$schema-note: Reader-facing tag policy, shared by the Python SSR and the Svelte SPA.
Both sides pick a story's kicker/breadcrumb from its tags, and they used to
hold separate lists: the backend skipped 6 labels, the frontend 18. On an
article tagged ["update", "defi"] the crawler was served "Update" and the
reader saw "DeFi" a frame later — same URL, two different sections.
After editing this file run:  python3 tools/design/sync_tokens.py --write
meta_tags_note: Provenance and pipeline labels. Fine as chips at the end of an article; never the kicker, because they say how we found the story rather than what it is about.
display_labels_note: Internal slug -> reader-facing text. DISPLAY ONLY: /topic/<tag> URLs always use the raw slug on both sides, so a link never changes shape based on this table.
